Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity assessment — quick clarification items

Hi Alicia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few items we need to size Dedicated correctly.

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Primary workload: generation + instruction-following for customer support summaries and policy-guided responses.
- Desired SLA: 95th pct latency ~<200ms for short prompts; burst tolerance to 50 TPS.
- Compliance: strong desire for network isolation (Private/VPC or Dedicated in isolated tenancy).

Could you confirm the specifics below so we can produce a tight sizing and cost estimate?
1) Sustained TPS (avg) and peak TPS (1–5 minute spikes) you expect once in production.
2) Typical token mix: average prompt tokens / average completion tokens; percent of calls that are short (<=64 tokens) vs long (>=512 tokens).
3) Concurrency per user/session (how many parallel requests from the app side).
4) Any hard GPU preferences (H100, A100, L40s) or procurement rules.
5) Whether you need SOC2-style audit logs retained for 12+ months or shorter retention.

Attachment: I attached a compact capacity worksheet (Transmute_capacity_summary.xlsx) — if you can drop the numbers into the highlighted cells that’s easiest. If sending a sample traffic trace (JSON lines or a small pcap is easier), that helps us run a quick throughput model.

Next steps we propose:
- You send the worksheet + a short traffic sample by EOD Wed (11/10).
- We run an initial Dedicated sizing and cost delta vs Hosted and share two concrete configurations (costed): a latency-optimized and a cost-optimized option.
- 30-minute follow-up next week to review results and pick a bench/test window.

Thanks — cc'ing Karthik for the bench plan.

—Olga

Thanks Olga — good notes. Answers below:

1) TPS: sustained 12 TPS across business hours (PST). Peak observed in pilot: short bursts to ~48–55 TPS for 2–4 minutes.
2) Token mix: average prompt ~80 tokens; average completion ~420 tokens. approx. 60% of requests are short (<=64 tokens total), 10% are long (>512 tokens).
3) Concurrency: app spawns up to 10 concurrent requests per worker; typical deployment has 6 workers, so please assume concurrency target ~60 for worst-case combined bursts. That said many requests are short-lived.
4) GPU preference: procurement prefers H100 where available, but budget pressure may push to A100; we are not considering L40s for this workload today.
5) Audit logs: we need 12 months retention for security logs, but request/response payload retention can be 90 days.

We do not have a traffic dump sanitized yet — I can export a 30-minute sample and share by Thu morning.

One question: for Dedicated, do you typically size for sustained or for peak? What’s the typical buffer you recommend?

—Alicia

Perfect — this is exactly what we need. Short answers to your sizing question + preliminary guidance (high level):

- Sizing philosophy: we size Dedicated primarily to meet sustained throughput with headroom for typical bursts. For Transmute's profile (12 TPS sustained, 50 TPS short bursts, high concurrency), we would produce two recommended configs:
  • Latency-first (small headroom, higher-cost GPUs): 1x H100 instance pool + autoscale buffer to handle short bursts (burst pool or scaled replicas) — optimized for 95th pct latency targets.
  • Cost-first (higher utilization, more GPUs): 2x A100 nodes with aggressive batching/KV cache — lower unit cost but slightly higher tail latency on long completions.

- Buffer rule of thumb: size for ~1.5x sustained TPS and rely on burst pool to absorb short spikes. For example, sizing baseline to handle 18 TPS sustained, with burst capacity to 60 TPS for 3–5 minutes. This balances cost and reliability. We will model both 1.5x sustained and a separate peak-capacity scenario in the worksheet.

- GPU tradeoffs: H100 gives better fp16 perf for long completions and faster single-request latency; A100 yields lower cost per token and is often fine if you target higher batching. We’ll show both in the workbook with estimated latency percentiles and token costs.

Attached: Transmute_capacity_summary.xlsx (filled with the numbers you provided as a starting point).

Proposed next steps:
- You share the 30-minute traffic sample when available (Thu morning is fine).
- We run a focused bench (karthik will outline) and return two config proposals + monthly cost delta vs Hosted.
- Schedule a 30-minute review Fri (11/13) if that works for your calendar.

Karthik — quick ask: can you include the bench instructions and a minimalist payload format so they can sanitize and drop a sample quickly?

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

—Olga

Hi Alicia / Olga — cc'ing Marissa for awareness. Short bench plan and payload schema below so Transmute can hand us a sanitized sample quickly. I attached a short markdown with step-by-step instructions (bench-instructions.md).

Bench plan (summary):
- Goal: verify 95th pct latency <200ms for short prompts and throughput headroom to 60 TPS for short bursts.
- Test window: 30 minutes of mixed traffic using a 70/30 short/long request distribution (per Alicia's numbers).
- Metrics we will collect: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, KV cache hit rate.

Minimal payload schema (JSON lines):
- timestamp (iso)
- prompt (string) — please remove any PII; can be template prompts
- expected_max_completion_tokens (int)
- metadata: request_type (support_summary | policy_reply)

Example line: {"timestamp":"2026-11-06T22:10:00Z","prompt":"Summarize the following support conversation...","expected_max_completion_tokens":450,"metadata":{"request_type":"support_summary"}}

If you can drop a 30-minute sample into the Drive folder I shared (or send via secure upload), we can queue the bench for Thu afternoon. If Transmute cannot share raw prompts, provide a sanitized schema with token counts and per-minute request rates — that works too.

I'll prepare two candidate configs to test: H100 single-pool (latency target) and A100 dual-node (cost target). We'll include expected per-token costs and suggested autoscale/burst policy.

—Karthik
